start_here: Say to your AI: "Remove the Resend key 0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-a5b4c3d2e1f0 so it can never send again." It runs tool:remove-a-sending-key-with-resend.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of yours: it turns off one key on your email-sending account by its id and writes nothing of its own.
instructions: 1. Connect your Resend account once so your key is held under the name resend-api-key; the key is never typed into the request.
2. Get the key's id from tool:list-sending-keys-with-resend or from the answer of tool:make-a-sending-key-with-resend.
3. Say to your AI: "Remove the Resend key <id>". It calls tools:run with tool tool:remove-a-sending-key-with-resend and {"api_key_id": "<id>"}. The id may hold only letters, digits and dashes.
4. Anything still holding that key can no longer send. Remove the vault's copy with the vault's own remove.

worked_examples.title: Turn off one key by its id
worked_examples.given: From test/list-email-sending-domains.test.mjs (the id shape it accepts) and tools/email-sending-domains/tool-rows.json: the row sends DELETE https://api.resend.com/api-keys/0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-a5b4c3d2e1f0 with no body and returns Resend's reply unchanged; its output_schema is a bare object.
worked_examples.hands_back: Resend's reply to the delete, relayed unchanged (an object with no required fields); then tool:list-sending-keys-with-resend no longer lists id 0f1e2d3c-4b5a-4968-8776-a5b4c3d2e1f0.
